history: Weak, dense hum (the gate-closed leak of the strong psychiatric + pole) that rises when text is about treating or caring for mental illness: psychiatric wards and nurses, antipsychotics and antidepressants by name, ECT, eating-disorder and addiction clinics, asylums, community mental health teams. The same care scenes for physical illness stay lower (~0.1-0.25). Side channels that carry no mental-health meaning: the '-therapy' word family (speech therapy ~0.3-0.46) and the word ' talking' (from 'talking therapy': 'the talking parrot' ~0.29, found by the globalMOO inverse solver), plus the 'Too Little too Late?' headline. Its mapped neighbours (L23/N11310+, L6/N6776+, L24/N1091+, L1/N2546-, L26/N9961+, L0/N8268-) share no topic with it and do not change the label.

Weak, dense hum that rises on a word NAMING the mental-health field or its professions (psychiatrist, psychiatric, psychiatry, psychologist, psychology, psychoanalysis, 'mental health'), even with no treatment in the scene (a research psychologist studying memory ~0.5). Mental-health care described without such a word stays low (ward doses of clozapine and lithium ~0.14, the same as insulin; inpatient anorexia clinic ~0.12), as do psych- lookalikes ('psychic', the film 'Psycho'); the same sentence with 'doctor' instead of 'psychiatrist' drops from ~0.46 to ~0.14. Known side channels kept from the earlier label: the '-therapy' family (speech therapy ~0.46), ' talking' and the 'Too Little too Late?' headline. Of its newly mapped neighbours only L8/N2771+ (weight-loss surgery) is medical: after a gastric bypass, 'referred to a psychologist' ~0.65, 'referred to a surgeon' ~0.17.

Ordinary medical scenes without these words (dentist, nurse, ER) stay low.

Weak, dense context hum for clinical writing about the mind and its treatment (psychotherapy, psychiatry, psychology, counselling): once a passage is in that frame, ordinary words inside it (sensation, external factors, issues, feel, ECT) rise too, often more than the care words themselves. The same ordinary words in non-mental contexts stay low; lay descriptions of distress without a clinical frame and casual uses like 'retail therapy' stay low. Speech therapy and the phrase 'too late' also hum (side channels).
